evidence.testTitle: MSG-027: disabled authority is rechecked on surviving sockets despite lost invalidation delivery
evidence.scenarioScope: Account disable revokes active access.
evidence.rationale: Independent integration mapping from explicitly reviewed operation assertions, not inferred from scenario tags or aggregate suite names.
assertionDetails: Disable commits with eager invalidation deliberately lost; original sockets are assertedOPEN and submit a forbidden frame without a conditional skip, production ingress rechecks authoritative account state and closes1000, no protected output or mutation occurs, and disabled authority stays revoked after recreation.

A second device can remain open after account-wide membership cleanup; if still OPEN its next PING triggers the unchanged credential recheck and closure, rather than assuming membership removal always immediately closes every socket.

evidence.testTitle: MSG-027: disabled authority is rechecked on surviving sockets despite lost invalidation delivery
evidence.scenarioScope: Account disable state survives runtime restart.
evidence.rationale: Independent integration mapping from explicitly reviewed operation assertions, not inferred from scenario tags or aggregate suite names.
assertionDetails: Real rootadmin disable stores Bob disabled_at; after disposing the controlled invalidation-loss runtime and recreating uninstrumented production, Bob bearer access remains401, Alice/unrelated messages survive and Bob has no added role.

All users and rootadmin are provisioned through genuine public registration/bootstrap/login on the frozen production runtime with unique passwords; original credentials and SQLite directory are reused by a copied-bundle Miniflare fixture.

The fixture subclasses only SessionDO.invalidateAccountPermissions to return 0, modeling lost eager invalidation delivery after Accounts committed disable; no authentication, dispatch, ingress, outbound permission checks, account storage or WebSocket attachment is overridden or fabricated.

Two independently authenticated Bob IRC sessions successfully publish/receive before disable, actual Bob event stream receives the control, Charlie admin disable is exactly 403, and genuine root disable is exactly 200 with ok=true and invalidatedSessions=0.

Both original Bob sockets are unconditionally asserted OPEN after committed disable; the original sender unconditionally sends PRIVMSG disabled-surviving-socket-publish and the unchanged production ingress check closes it with code 1000/reason Account no longer available.

Existing Bob REST append is exactly 401; Alice private post still reaches authorized IRC/event recipients, while Bob receiver/event stream and unrelated Charlie IRC/event stream receive no private content and no stream receives forbidden publish content.

A second device can remain open after account-wide membership cleanup; if still OPEN its next PING triggers the unchanged credential recheck and closure, rather than assuming membership removal always immediately closes every socket.

After actual fixture disposal, SQLite contains no disabled IRC/REST publish, retains original/unrelated/Alice-new message authors and bodies, stores Bob disabled_at with Alice enabled, preserves root admin role and empty Bob/custom-channel role assignments; a new uninstrumented production runtime keeps Bob REST at 401 and retains legitimate/unrelated history.

evidence.testTitle: matrix media r2 MEDIA-001 MEDIA-002 MEDIA-003 MEDIA-006 MEDIA-013 MEDIA-014 private ownership and deletion persist
evidence.scenarioScope: Independent Alice and Bob upload distinct bytes; authenticated owner reads succeed, anonymous upload/download is 401, other-user and guessed-ID reads are 404 without Alice bytes, and Bob cannot delete Alice media.
evidence.rationale: Executable real Miniflare/workerd, genuine public-registration credentials, actual IRC/REST and stopped SQLite evidence; scope and omissions are explicit.
assertionDetails: Independent Alice and Bob upload distinct bytes; authenticated owner reads succeed, anonymous upload/download is 401, other-user and guessed-ID reads are 404 without Alice bytes, and Bob cannot delete Alice media.
Authorized Alice delete makes the canonical /media URL and download/query-token variants 404; unrelated Bob bytes remain readable.
Real IRC observers are synchronized with PING before observation and receive only the final PONG, with no media publication.
After workerd shutdown SQLite contains exactly Bob metadata with correct owner/size/provider; R2 tests independently inspect real bucket object bytes/list/delete (SQLite stores no R2 payload).
SQLite provider additionally reconstructs workerd and verifies deletion stays effective and Bob bytes remain accessible only to Bob.

evidence.testTitle: MSG-013: IRC +ircord/edit cross-author edit has no persistent or recipient effects
evidence.scenarioScope: Alice can edit her own message when editing is permitted.
evidence.rationale: Exact passed test on frozen bundle 06; assertionDetails describe its contribution, not all behaviors of every transport.
assertionDetails: IRC +ircord/edit targets cross-author; all three aliases are executed separately through IRC PRIVMSG and REST POST tags, using real members and a foreign secret-channel row.

IRC returns exactly 404 with "Cannot send to channel (+n)" for inaccessible targets or "You can only edit your own existing messages" otherwise; REST returns exactly 403 membership-required for inaccessible channel or 400 own-existing-message error otherwise.

After event/IRC barriers, no forbidden body, message.updated or message.deleted event reaches any stream; neither recipient receives the attempted edit. Alice is the channel founder but still cannot edit Bob.
Authorized author control using the same alias updates Alice's root and sends editor=alice/newContent=legitimate-irc-edit only to member event streams and the member IRC recipient.

Channel info including founder/memberCount/modes and role definitions stay identical; SQLite account_roles and channel_user_roles stay empty, sender IDs and Bob/Charlie originals remain intact, forbidden body is absent, and the edited root survives runtime recreation.

evidence.testTitle: message denial boundaries MSG-007: cross-author edit is rejected without mutation or delivery
evidence.scenarioScope: Alice cannot edit Bob's message.
evidence.rationale: Exact passed test on frozen bundle 06; assertionDetails describe its contribution, not all behaviors of every transport.
assertionDetails: cross-author edit is rejected without mutation or delivery.
Public registration/login created Alice, Bob and Charlie with unique passwords; channel members made original messages in #history and unrelated secret #private.

REST PATCH/DELETE returned exactly 403: cross-author edit uses "You can only edit your own messages"; inaccessible edit uses "Channel membership is required"; missing/foreign edit uses "Message not found"; redaction uses "You are not authorized to redact this message" or "Message does not exist or has already been redacted" as applicable.
Corresponding IRC edit PRIVMSG returns 404 with +n or own-existing-message error; IRC REDACT returns FAIL REDACT REDACT_FORBIDDEN or UNKNOWN_MSGID. Error bodies exclude original content.

Both channels' REST info (including memberCount/founder/modes) and role definitions stay identical; no forbidden update/delete events reach any of three real event streams and no recipient receives forbidden IRC mutation output.
SQLite retains all three original unredacted rows; separate recreated Miniflare runtime independently reads both histories with unrelated content preserved.

evidence.testTitle: message denial boundaries MSG-007: cross-author edit is rejected without mutation or delivery
evidence.scenarioScope: Unauthorized edits produce no data changes or events.
evidence.rationale: Exact passed test on frozen bundle 06; assertionDetails describe its contribution, not all behaviors of every transport.
assertionDetails: cross-author edit is rejected without mutation or delivery.
Public registration/login created Alice, Bob and Charlie with unique passwords; channel members made original messages in #history and unrelated secret #private.

REST PATCH/DELETE returned exactly 403: cross-author edit uses "You can only edit your own messages"; inaccessible edit uses "Channel membership is required"; missing/foreign edit uses "Message not found"; redaction uses "You are not authorized to redact this message" or "Message does not exist or has already been redacted" as applicable.
Corresponding IRC edit PRIVMSG returns 404 with +n or own-existing-message error; IRC REDACT returns FAIL REDACT REDACT_FORBIDDEN or UNKNOWN_MSGID. Error bodies exclude original content.

Both channels' REST info (including memberCount/founder/modes) and role definitions stay identical; no forbidden update/delete events reach any of three real event streams and no recipient receives forbidden IRC mutation output.
SQLite retains all three original unredacted rows; separate recreated Miniflare runtime independently reads both histories with unrelated content preserved.

evidence.testTitle: [AUTH-022 DM-015 WS-024] logout invalidates an idle receiving event credential and preserves independent authorization
evidence.scenarioScope: API logout, administrator disable/reenable, or administrator password reset while the receiving clients remain idle.
evidence.rationale: Exact Vitest test completed; only the listed assertions are credited. Other dimensions remain required and uncovered unless another matched test covers them.
assertionDetails: Independent credentials authenticate the founder, recipient, outsider and administrator; the recipient receives private IRC/event and DM controls before revocation.

The selected revocation invalidates the old REST and DM credential and closes its event stream before later private delivery; disable/reset also close the independent IRC login, while API logout deliberately preserves independently authenticated IRC access.
The legitimate founder still receives the private event, an outsider receives the public output marker without private contents, and unrelated stored messages remain intact.
Reenable does not reactivate the old token; fresh permitted login works, and SQLite contains exactly one replacement Bob API session and one committed post-revocation message.

evidence.rationale: Exact Vitest test completed; only the listed assertions are credited. Other dimensions remain required and uncovered unless another matched test covers them.
assertionDetails: Before revocation Bob receives the private IRC message and event; the unrelated account cannot perform the same admin mutation and protected history remains unchanged.
